While the Raiders and Bills were tied 13-13 at halftime, the Las Vegas offense saw a chance to get going, following the departure of C.J. Gardner-Johnson.

In the middle of the second quarter, Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the Raiders and Bills game because he was seen spitting towards members of the Raiders offensive line.

CJ Gardner-Johnson just did a Jalen Carter and spit on a player.He was ejected pic.twitter.com/C6BALpIABj

Gardner-Johnson was seen walking towards Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum and guard Spencer Burford and started to exchange some words with them, resulting in him spitting at them.

Buffalo received a 14-yard penalty for Gardner-Johnson’s actions.

Through the first half, both teams were nearly matching each other’s production as the Bills finished with 176 total yards of offense while Las Vegas finished with 175.

At halftime, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins was 12 of 17 for 126 yards, while running back Ashton Jeanty had eight carries for 27 yards and a touchdown on a one-yard run in the first quarter.

Las Vegas scored two more times in the first half from two field goals that came off the leg of kicker Matt Gay.

Gardner-Johnson’s incident resulted in Las Vegas having another opportunity to add points before halftime as Gay was able to nail a 27-yard field goal through the uprights.

Buffalo got on the board first in the game when kicker Tyler Bass hit a 44-yard field goal on the Bills’ opening possession. Bass had another field goal early in the second quarter from a 28-yard kick.

The Bills’ first touchdown of the game was a 9-yard touchdown pass from Josh Allen to Khalil Shakir with 7:13 in the second quarter.

In the middle of the third quarter, the Bills were able to hold a 23-13 lead over the Raiders without Gardner-Johnson on the field.

Taylor Swift stepped out with Caitlin Clark and Este Haim to support her husband, Travis Kelce, at the Kansas City Chiefs vs. Los Angeles Chargers game.

The “Lover” songstress — showing her team spirit in red — appeared in good spirits while chatting with Clark and Haim in a VIP suite at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, on Sunday.

The trio attentively watched the match while surrounded by other spectators.

At one point, Swift, 36, was photographed giving Travis’ mom, Donna Kelce, a big hug upon the latter’s arrival. The matriarch proudly wore a bedazzled Chiefs jacket.

As for the Grammy winner, she wore a red turtleneck sweater and her iconic red lip for the outing.

The hitmaker jetted off to Kansas City to support Travis, 37, after she attended the 2026 Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles on Saturday night.

Swift had a Cinderella moment as she stepped out on the red carpet in a Dior pale blue dress for the star-studded night.

The hitmaker later changed into a blue Ralph Lauren-designed dress and Cartier jewelry while performing at the venue.

The “Cruel Summer” singer took the stage to perform a slew of bangers from her career, including her “Toy Story 5″ track “I Knew It, I Knew You” (2026), “The Fate of Ophelia” (2025), “Blank Space” (2014) and “Love Story” (2008).

Swift attended the night solo as Travis geared up to take the field. The tight end’s NFL schedule also forced him to miss the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards last month, at which Swift was awarded the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors.

The pop princess, meanwhile, has attended several of Travis’ home games, with her last sighting being at the Chiefs vs. Indianapolis Colts match on Sept. 20.

At the time, Swift proudly cheered as the NFL star scored his first touchdown of the season, as she pointed to her wedding ring and appeared to have said, “That’s my husband!” The Chiefs ultimately beat the Colts 33 to 30 in overtime.

Swift and Travis wed in a star-studded ceremony at Madison Square Garden on July 3, and the latter has referred to it as “the best night of [his] life.”

Travis praised MSG for going “above and beyond” to create the “intimate and genuine setting” he and Swift wanted during the Sept. 2 “New Heights” episode.

Since tying the knot, the duo have stepped out for several date nights, with their most recent sighting being at Old Rose in NYC earlier this month.

news.originalContent:

Anthropic said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, subject to stockholder approval, with the stake potentially increasing as the artificial intelligence giant’s valuation grows.

The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic’s shares, at the board’s discretion, for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on workers.

The company said none of the equity held by the fund would be used for lobbying or political contributions in the US or abroad.

The maker of the Claude AI assistant is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors.

The company, which has positioned itself as safety-first, has often highlighted risks associated with its AI models, most recently in its IPO prospectus, which it said could exhibit “self-preserving behaviors,” Reuters reported exclusively in September.

Taken together with the new fund, roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares would be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares that could be allocated if it reaches future valuation milestones.

Anthropic said it would disclose further details in coming months on the fund’s governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.
news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. Anthropic روز یکشنبه اعلام کرد که 5٪ از سهام خود را به یک صندوق جدید منافع عمومی، مشروط به تایید سهامداران، متعهد می کند، که با افزایش ارزش گذاری غول هوش مصنوعی، این سهام به طور بالقوه افزایش می یابد. صندوق پیشنهادی به‌عنوان یک شرکت کاملاً با مسئولیت محدود تأسیس می‌شود و به ازای هر 50 درصد افزایش در ارزش شرکت بالاتر از سطح پایه که هنوز فاش نشده است، 2 درصد از سهام آنتروپیک را به صلاحدید هیئت‌مدیره دریافت می‌کند. این شرکت گفت که هیچ یک از سهام در اختیار صندوق برای لابی گری یا مشارکت های سیاسی در ایالات متحده یا خارج از کشور استفاده نمی شود. سازنده دستیار هوش مصنوعی کلود در حال برنامه ریزی برای یکی از بزرگترین عرضه های اولیه در تاریخ به عنوان یک شرکت منفعت عمومی است، ساختاری قانونی که مدیریت را ملزم می کند تا منافع گسترده تری را در نظر بگیرد و همچنین برای سرمایه گذاران سود کند. این شرکت که خود را در جایگاه اول ایمنی قرار داده است، اغلب خطرات مرتبط با مدل های هوش مصنوعی خود را برجسته کرده است، اخیراً در دفترچه عرضه اولیه سهام خود که به گفته رویترز منحصراً در ماه سپتامبر گزارش داده می تواند "رفتارهای خود را حفظ کند" را برجسته کرده است. با در نظر گرفتن صندوق جدید، تقریباً 20 درصد از سهام آنتروپیک به اهداف عمومی اختصاص داده می شود.

Courteney Cox proves age is just a number.

During a recent trip to Hawaii to celebrate her friend, Jennifer Meyer’s wedding, the 62-year-old actress was spotted enjoying a day at the beach.

The “Cougar Town” star was photographed smiling in a black bikini while standing on the beach.

She paired the bikini with layered gold necklaces and earrings, and wore her hair in a ponytail to take a dip in the ocean. In the photos, she is seen standing knee-deep in the water before wrapping a towel over her body to dry off.

Cox has shared how she manages to stay fit as she gets older, telling Marie Claire in September 2022 that she takes vitamins in the mornings, in addition to drinking “the cucumber, pineapple, ginger, and lemon thing.”

“I play tennis twice a week. I used to box twice a week, but my left knee is hurt,” she said about her fitness routine. “I also do pilates once a week. As I get older, I realize it’s more important for me to do weights. It’s amazing how I used to be really muscley but not so much anymore.”

She later gave fans a glimpse of her workout routine in an Instagram video in July 2024, which showed her running on a treadmill, pull-ups, squats and crunches.

The “Friends” star was also seen enjoying her summer while on a luxury yacht off the Spanish island of Mallorca with her longtime friend, Jennifer Aniston, and other actors, including Judd Apatow, Leslie Mann and Pedro Pascal.

In addition to relaxing on the boat, the celebrity besties were also photographed taking a dip in the ocean and engaging in water sports.

Cox rose to stardom as one of the stars of the hit sitcom “Friends,” which she starred in for 10 seasons from 1994 to 2004, alongside Aniston, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer, Matt LeBlanc and Matthew Perry.

Following Perry’s death in October 2023, Cox shared on “CBS Sunday Morning,” that Perry was “probably one of the funniest human beings in the world.”

“I’m so thankful I got to work so closely with him for so many years,” she said. “He visits me a lot, if we believe in that.”

She further shared some of her spiritual connections to other lost loved ones, like her parents, and how she still feels Perry with her.

“I’ve talked to my mom, my dad, Matthew. I feel like there are a lot of people that are… I think they guide us. I do sense, yeah, I sense Matthew’s around for sure,” Cox said.

A married HR executive at a California school district allegedly waged a relentless campaign of sexual harassment, threats, and coercion against a subordinate, threatening his family, pressuring him into sex, and secretly topping up his slashed wages using a Target card, an explosive lawsuit has claimed.

According to court documents filed in the Superior Court of California, Ja’Vance Coleman — a 42-year-old former NBA prospect at Fresno State — claims he was subjected to sexual harassment, racial discrimination, and retaliation by former Fresno Unified School District HR director Manjit Atwal.

Official court filings show the civil lawsuit, which brings nine causes of action against Atwal and the district, has been assigned to Judge Jonathan M. Skiles in Department 503 of the Fresno Superior Court.

According to the suit obtained by The Post, Coleman was first hired by the district in January 2023 as a noontime assistant at Columbia Elementary School before landing a role within FUSD’s main human resources department later that spring.

The legal papers allege Atwal quickly propositioned her new subordinate for sexual favors. According to the complaint, Atwal had established a “pattern of threatening the jobs or job-related benefits of black employees in exchange for sexual acts,” leaving Coleman to believe that refusing her advances would lead to immediate firing or reprisals.

The suit alleges Atwal became “territorial,” falsely accusing female co-workers of flirting with Coleman and moving his desk to isolate him from other staff.

According to the suit, after other employees and administrators began suspecting the harassment, FUSD transferred Coleman to Tatarian Elementary School as a campus safety assistant, cutting his pay from $35 an hour to $25 an hour.

The filing alleges Atwal then stepped in to cover the pay drop herself, secretly supplementing his income with off-the-books cash and purchases made on her personal Target credit card “so that her husband would not notice”.

According to the complaint, when an internal investigation into the hostile work environment began, Atwal allegedly offered Coleman a $300 bribe to lie to investigators and deny that any sexual relationship or harassment had occurred.

The lawsuit asserts that when Coleman eventually refused her advances near the end of 2025, Atwal allegedly retaliated against him.

According to court papers, the HR boss showed up at the house owned by Coleman’s mother, repeatedly drove past his home, and threatened his family.

The suit alleges she warned him that if anyone learned of their relationship, his district-employed relatives would lose their jobs, and his high school basketball star son, who plays point guard, would be blocked from graduating or attending college.

In another allegation detailed in the filing, Atwal allegedly accused Coleman of stealing her jewelry and sent him a news article detailing the lynching of a black man in a local park.

The complaint alleges top FUSD executives knew about Atwal’s conduct but failed to take immediate action to protect him.

Before transitioning into a school district role, Coleman was a prominent local athlete in the Central Valley, starring at Washington Union High School before playing three seasons for the Fresno State Bulldogs from 2004 to 2007, earning All-WAC honors.

Following the suit’s filing, former district employees have spoken out regarding Atwal’s workplace behavior.

In a social media statement, former FUSD office assistant Carla Sewell claimed Atwal had “been like this for years,” recalling an incident where the former HR executive “began screaming and yelling at me to the point where she was asked to leave the room.”

“Toxic management and higher-ups who create unhealthy work environments should not be allowed to continue without consequences,” Sewell said.

According to court records, FUSD eventually placed Atwal on extended paid administrative leave for nearly an entire school year before informing her that if she did not resign, the district would fire her.

An FUSD spokesperson said while the district cannot comment on pending litigation or confidential personnel matters, it takes all allegations of harassment and discrimination seriously, confirming Ms Atwal is no longer employed by the district.

Taylor Swift made the trip from LA to Missouri to support husband Travis Kelce as Chiefs take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.

She was shown, alongside Fever star Caitlin Clark, on the CBS broadcast cheering on the Chiefs tight end after a catch over the middle for a big game in the second quarter. The duo previously watched the Chiefs take on the Texans at Arrowhead Stadium in January 2025.

The Chiefs had a bye last week, and Kelce and Swift celebrated the All-Pro tight end’s 37th birthday in New York.

Swift sparkled in a custom Dior gown for her first appearance at the Academy Museum Gala, which raises money for the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures, on Saturday night.

Taylor Swift loves what she is seeing. pic.twitter.com/vxEhz65591

The 14-time Grammy winner performed her 2025 song “The Fate of Ophelia” for the very first time, and her contender for the 2027 Oscars, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Pixar film “Toy Story 5″ — as well as her hit, “Love Story” which was released in 2008, and 2014’s “Blank Space.”

She made an outfit change for her stage performance and donned a navy blue dress from Ralph Lauren Spring 27 runway, which included a smocked bodice, drop waist, and crystal-embellished pleated tulle.

Swift was not in attendance for the Chiefs’ divisional win over the Raiders, 30-27, last week after she made a surprise appearance on “Saturday Night Live” in New York and crashed host Dakota Johnson’s opening monologue.

She missed the Chiefs’ 24-10 road win against the Miami Dolphins to attend the MTV Video Music Awards, during which she was honored with the inaugural Artist Director Honors and Video of the Year for “The Fate of Ophelia” on Sept. 27.

Swift was in Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium when the Chiefs beat the Broncos 31-10 in Week 1, followed by a 33-30 overtime victory against the Colts in Week 2.

The pair were married on July 3 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, nearly a year after getting engaged.

news.originalContent:
Alberta’s independence movement faces likely defeat, but history suggests losing a referendum may not end the fight.

Cory Morgan has spent more than 25 years fighting for Canada’s oil-rich province of Alberta to become an independent country. On Monday, Albertans will head to the polls to vote on the issue for the very first time. But even if the answer is no, Morgan said he’s in it for the long haul.

“I would respect the will of the voters,” he told Al Jazeera. “If they’ve decided it’s not time to go that route yet, then so be it. But that doesn’t mean I’ll stop.”

Morgan, the founder of the advocacy organisation Pathway to Independence, is among a group of longtime separatists who have managed to push what was once a fringe idea onto the ballot.

Monday’s provincial referendum asks Alberta residents to weigh whether they would like to pursue a binding resolution in the future on the question of independence.

Polls indicate the pro-independence side has little chance of succeeding, with four of five people in the province saying they want Alberta to remain a part of Canada. But Morgan’s focus is on the one in five who don’t.

“That’s not a movement that’s leaving,” he said.

What the referendum will mean for the separatist movement and for Canada as a whole, however, is a more complicated question.

Monday’s ballot gives Albertans two options: to remain part of Canada or begin the legal process for holding a future referendum on separation.

A vote in favour of the second option doesn’t mean Alberta immediately becomes an independent country.

Any province that tries to secede would first have to go through complex negotiations with the federal government in Ottawa, other provinces and Indigenous peoples who live in and around Alberta.

Some separatist organisers have been using that distinction to encourage people to vote for the referendum — even if they don’t necessarily want independence.

“Strategic separatists and their leaders have been using that ambiguity, that lower-bar threshold, to entice folks to vote not to leave, but rather to send Ottawa a message that Albertans need to be heard,” said Jared Wesley, a political science professor at the University of Alberta.

He told Al Jazeera that the message may be resonating with some voters.

Data collected by Viewpoint Alberta, a University of Alberta-based research initiative, suggests that two-thirds of voters who support the referendum say they’re doing so for strategic reasons, to send a message to Ottawa.

These are people Morgan calls “reluctant separatists”, people who are “at the end of their rope” and simply want Ottawa to pay attention.

But Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned Albertans against this strategy.

“Don’t be fooled by the idea you can ‘send a message’ with your vote,” he told a pro-Canada rally in Calgary on Thursday. “This is not poker. A vote against Canada is a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division and great uncertainty.”

Monday’s referendum has been decades in the making. Separatists have long felt that Alberta, home to the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves, sends too much money to Ottawa, subsidising the rest of the country while receiving little in return.

They also take issue with federal energy policies that they feel limit the potential of the province’s oil industry.

For Morgan, the resentment stretches back to the 1980s when the National Energy Program was introduced by the government of Pierre Trudeau, former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau’s father.

The policy used price controls, taxes and ownership rules to keep Canadian energy affordable while directing more of Alberta’s revenues to Ottawa.

It has since become a central symbol of “Western alienation”, a term used to describe the sense of disenfranchisement felt among Canada’s westernmost provinces.

Those tensions resurfaced decades later under Justin Trudeau, whose term began in 2015. His climate policies, including a national carbon tax and a limit on emissions, angered Alberta’s oil sector.

“We’ve been fighting about the same things for 50 years,” said Morgan.

Then came the COVID-19 pandemic. Experts say demonstrations against health restrictions mobilised a new generation of conservative activists, breathing new life into Alberta’s separatist movement.

Trudeau ultimately resigned as Liberal Party leader and prime minister in 2025, amid sinking poll numbers. Carney was elected his replacement.

Last year, under growing pressure from separatist groups, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith’s government made it easier to start referendums, helping bring the question of Alberta’s independence onto the political agenda.

For Wesley, the moment is less about growing public support for independence and more about pressure from within Smith’s governing United Conservative Party, whose members show higher support for separation than Albertans generally.

“We’re having a referendum because Danielle Smith wants us to have a referendum,” Wesley said. “She is looking to solve internal party matters by throwing a question to the broader public.”

Though she called Monday’s referendum, Smith has said she opposes the independence effort, and on October 14, she announced she had voted against seceding.

“In my view, now is not the time to give up hope in our country, not when we have fought so long and come so far,” Smith said in a social media video, explaining her vote.

Smith’s political gamble has drawn comparisons with the 2016 Brexit referendum in the United Kingdom, including from Carney.

At the time, then-UK Prime Minister David Cameron called a vote over whether the country should leave the European Union, in hopes of settling a debate dividing his own Conservative Party.

Voters ultimately chose to leave the bloc, triggering years of political unrest.

But Ian Cooper, a political scientist who grew up in Alberta and now lives in Ireland, says a more useful comparison might be a different UK referendum in 1975, when British voters chose overwhelmingly to stay in what was then known as the European Economic Community.

That vote, he said, did little to deter those who wanted the country out.

“The activists who were in favour of Brexit — this is before anybody called it Brexit — they really played the long game,” he said. “It took them 25 years, but they finally achieved it.”

Cooper suspects that, even if Alberta separation is roundly defeated, separatists could take a similar approach, pursuing the issue over the long term to gain prominence and support.

“My impression is that they really are true believers, and it’s really ideologically driven,” he said.

If Monday’s separatist vote fails, Morgan said separatists would need to take a hard look at why they had fallen short and work towards making a stronger case for independence in the future.

He does not believe the underlying grievances can be resolved by working within the Canadian system or by electing a more sympathetic federal government.

Carney, who grew up in Alberta, acknowledged at Thursday’s rally that “the frustrations that many Albertans have felt are real”. He added that Ottawa had made people in the province feel “like our resources weren’t our own”.

The prime minister has tried, amid an ongoing trade war with the United States, to improve relations with Alberta, including through commitments to building a new pipeline to Canada’s west coast and major infrastructure projects.

Morgan admits that, for those whose goal is simply to get more leverage in Ottawa, “it’s pretty clear the movement has been effective”.

“We’ve seen more love from a federal prime minister in the last year than we’ve seen in the last 10,” Morgan said. “The problem though, when it comes to stubborn independence folks like me, is nothing has changed in the system.”

Prime ministers come and go, he added. “We’re just one election away from another hostile one.”

But the referendum could also offer an opportunity to challenge the premise that Alberta’s grievances cannot be addressed within Canada.

The independence question is just one of 10 on Monday’s ballot. Other proposals include restricting temporary residents’ access to healthcare and education, as well as allowing Alberta to choose its own judges.

Smith has encouraged Albertans to vote in favour of the nine other proposals, arguing that they will give her more negotiating power in Ottawa.

“Many Albertans I speak with tell me they want to send Ottawa a message, and I would suggest the best way to do that is to give us a strong mandate on the other nine questions,” she said on social media.

If Albertans back those proposals but Ottawa refuses to make concessions, Cooper, the political scientist, said the movement would have fresh ammunition to argue that meaningful change within the current system is impossible.

“Buried in the nine other questions are the seeds for a future referendum,” Cooper added.

Not everyone agrees, however, on whether the separatists can emerge from the vote as a united force.

Wesley explained that people have been drawn to the separatist cause for a variety of reasons.

If there’s a sense that independence is not a realistic prospect, there may be little to keep that group of activists together, he said. They could turn their attention to other conservative issues, such as immigration.

Other experts question whether Alberta’s separatist movement, which is united more by economic grievances than by a shared cultural identity, can endure the way Quebec’s has.

Just two weeks ago, the largely French-speaking province elected the separatist Party Quebecois, which has promised a third referendum on independence after Trump leaves office.

Morgan, however, argues that Alberta does have a distinct culture, shaped by generations of people who have moved to the province in search of prosperity.

“The type of person drawn to do that is often an individualistic type of person,” he said. “They want the opportunity to go out and succeed or fail on their own.”

“And that builds a kind of a distinct culture on its own, even if it’s not a long-built one, as you would see in a distinct area like Quebec with a linguistic difference or in another country.”

Even if Albertans reject separation, he believes the movement has succeeded in forcing Ottawa to take the province’s frustrations more seriously.

“Hopefully some people understand that eventually something has to give,” he said. “So whatever the results are … I do hope, at the very least, they’ve served as a wake-up call to a lot of people.”

جنبش استقلال آلبرتا احتمالاً با شکست مواجه خواهد شد، اما تاریخ نشان می دهد که شکست در همه پرسی ممکن است نبرد را پایان دهد. کوری مورگان بیش از 25 سال را صرف مبارزه برای استان نفت خیز آلبرتا در کانادا کرده است تا به کشوری مستقل تبدیل شود. روز دوشنبه، آلبرتایی ها برای اولین بار به پای صندوق های رای می روند تا در مورد این موضوع رای دهند. اما حتی اگر پاسخ منفی باشد، مورگان گفت که برای مدت طولانی در این کار است. او به الجزیره گفت: «من به اراده رأی دهندگان احترام می گذارم. "اگر آنها تصمیم گرفته اند که هنوز زمان آن فرا نرسیده است، پس همینطور باشد. اما این بدان معنا نیست که من متوقف خواهم شد."
مورگان، بنیانگذار سازمان حمایت از مسیر استقلال، در میان گروهی از جدایی طلبان قدیمی است که توانسته اند ایده های حاشیه ای را به صندوق رای دهند. همه پرسی استانی روز دوشنبه از ساکنان آلبرتا می خواهد تا بررسی کنند که آیا مایلند در آینده یک قطعنامه الزام آور در مورد مسئله استقلال دنبال کنند یا خیر. نظرسنجی ها نشان می دهد که حزب طرفدار استقلال شانس کمی برای موفقیت دارد و چهار نفر از پنج نفر در این استان می گویند که می خواهند آلبرتا بخشی از کانادا باقی بماند. اما تمرکز مورگان روی یکی از پنج نفری است که این کار را نمی کنند. او گفت: «این جنبشی نیست که می رود. با این حال، همه پرسی برای جنبش جدایی طلب و برای کل کانادا چه معنایی خواهد داشت، سوال پیچیده تری است. رای روز دوشنبه دو گزینه را در اختیار آلبرتی ها قرار می دهد: باقی ماندن بخشی از کانادا یا آغاز روند قانونی برگزاری رفراندوم آینده در مورد جدایی. رأی به نفع دومی.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by ARMIN WEIGEL/AFP via Getty Images)

American companies are building batteries, hydrogen drones and homegrown fuel that could keep U.S. troops powered if a war cuts off foreign supply.

Companies showed off their equipment at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting, which ended Oct. 14. Attacks on merchant ships around the Strait of Hormuz had hit their highest point since the Iran war began, Reuters reported Oct. 14, citing independent data. (RELATED: Tanker Data Suggests There May Be Fewer Barrels Crossing Hormuz Than Thought)

“The days of secure and predictable logistics environments are over,” Army Lt. Gen. Mark Simerly, director of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA), said at the 2026 Defense Logistics & Energy Summit in September, according to an agency news release. He added that energy and fuel “will be high-value targets and decisive factors in operational success.”

Assistant Secretary of the Army for Installations, Energy and Environment Jordan Gillis told a House Armed Services subcommittee in March that in the Indo-Pacific “fuel logistics and vulnerable island locations present unique energy challenges,” according to his written testimony.

“From March-September 2026, DLA Energy purchased approximately 2.17 billion gallons of fuel, primarily to support the Department of War, and sold approximately 122.7 million gallons to support the U.S. Army,” the DLA’s energy arm said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation.

“DLA Energy’s global posture allows the agency to adapt to market shifts and geopolitical events, ensuring security in the supply of fuels,” the agency added. “Fuels are sourced close to the location of the requirement to meet Warfighter demands.”

GM Defense, a General Motors subsidiary, showed a prototype of its EPIQ Hybrid at the meeting. The system pairs a battery with a generator to cut heat and noise in remote areas, according to a company release.

Diesel generators “consume a lot of diesel, and diesel is a risk in a logistical environment,” a GM Defense representative told the DCNF at the company’s booth.

In the company’s setup, the generator charges the battery and then shuts off so the battery can carry the load, he added.

In the system’s hybrid mode, GM Defense has seen fuel savings of about 50 percent and about 80 percent less generator run time, a company representative said.

GM Defense built the EPIQ Hybrid for a 2023 Defense Innovation Unit program aimed at “reducing logistical requirements and the reliance on fossil fuels as the primary energy source across the DoD,” according to a company announcement. The Army and the Marines are now testing units, a company representative said.

The system is built from the same kind of battery modules GM uses in its electric vehicles, the representative said.

“GM is manufacturing vehicles at the gigawatt scale, and with that massive supply chain, there is a severe reduction in risk on that supply chain,” he told the DCNF.

Starting in 2028, federal law bars the Pentagon from buying advanced batteries for new programs whose key parts come from a “foreign entity of concern,” according to the U.S. Code. GM Defense’s batteries already meet those limits, a company representative told the DCNF.

Heven AeroTech, based in Sterling, Virginia, holds an Army agreement that lets units order its hydrogen-powered Z1 drone and the equipment that makes hydrogen to fuel it, according to a company release.

“Hydrogen-powered systems offer extended endurance, logistical flexibility, and reduced dependency on traditional fuel and battery supply chains,” Michael Buscher, the company’s president of U.S. operations, said in the release.

Commando Fuels, a New York company, says on its website that it was founded by veterans and makes fuel from “domestically-grown biomass.”

“Defense, maritime, and industrial operators need reliable domestic alternatives that can be certified and deployed quickly,” the company says on its “Why Now” page, adding that modular refining strengthens supply chains “by producing fuel closer to where it is needed.”

Michael Coleman, the company’s founder and CEO, told the DCNF in a phone interview that its goal is to let military bases keep running “when the main grid goes down” without relying on outside fuel trucks or civilian power grids.

Fuel made close to a base means “you’re not reliant on global supply chains to support your energy needs at a military installation,” Coleman said.

The company is working with the Pentagon’s research and engineering office to get its fuel to the point where it can power “a tank, a Humvee, and any other type of military vehicle without having to retrofit it,” he said.

Its next step is “multiple pilots that are being discussed through the Department of War,” Coleman added.

Coleman said the company could “move quickly and scale the energy needs of the military when needed” and that its fuel “will eventually be cheaper and more secure” than diesel.

“Commando is focusing strategically on fuel that grows in your backyard and powers your car in your front yard,” he said.

The company is also working with Native American and Amish communities that Coleman said “would never have a seat at the energy race.”

The Army also awarded GM Defense, Ford and BC Customs agreements in June to build prototypes of a heavier Infantry Squad Vehicle that can export enough power to run drone-defense and electronic warfare gear, Military Times reported.

“One of the things that we do have a critical capability gap on right now is power generation at that mobile brigade combat team level,” Jess Tolleson, the Army’s principal deputy assistant secretary for acquisition, logistics and technology, told senators in June, according to the outlet. (RELATED: America Has Little Fuel Cushion Left If A Hurricane Knocks Out Gulf Coast Refineries)

Oshkosh Defense’s eJLTV, a hybrid-electric tactical vehicle the company developed, shuts its engine off when it is not needed while an onboard battery keeps communications and other critical systems running, the company said in a statement to the DCNF.

“From a fuel efficiency standpoint, we’re seeing 20 to 30 percent fuel savings over mission profiles,” the company added. “When you’re standing outside the eJLTV in silent drive mode, all you hear is gravel.”

Oshkosh Defense is also helping Michigan Technological University develop a power kit that lets an Army medium tactical truck, the FMTV A2, supply electricity in the field. The kit “reduces the fuel deliveries required to sustain electrical power in remote locations,” and the company said the government is set to begin assessing the first two prototypes in the first three months of 2027.

“Protecting fuel and water are two of the most critical logistic challenges for the warfighter,” Kate Putland-Moss, group communications director for Parker Hannifin’s aerospace group, said in a statement to the DCNF.

The company’s Fuel Jerry Can is a portable pump that “removes sediment and water from contaminated fuel” and “fits on any vehicle,” which “is especially critical when units must lean on a local economy for fuel supply,” she said.

Parker’s electric motors and inverters drive vehicles, generate power and run hydraulics on “many defense platforms,” and the company’s cooling technology “allows for maximum fuel savings on the vehicle,” Putland-Moss added.

Engine and generator maker Cummins is seeing “increasing demand for both higher-capacity power generation and hybrid power solutions” as military bases and field sites add counter-drone systems, sensors and communications gear, a company spokesperson said in a statement to the DCNF.

Hybrid systems that pair generators with batteries can help by “reducing generator runtime, lowering fuel consumption and enabling quieter operation when mission requirements demand it,” the spokesperson said.

Cummins said it does not know of any Army tests that ran the service’s Advanced Medium Mobile Power Sources generators on renewable or synthetic diesel, but the company’s G-Drive power generation engines are approved to run on renewable diesel, the spokesperson added. Cummins testing shows those engines can run on 100 percent renewable diesel, regular diesel or a blend “while delivering performance comparable to conventional diesel operation,” according to the statement.

New Use Energy Solutions, an Arizona company building what it calls personal energy nodes, portable battery units, for the Army under an agreement with the Defense Innovation Unit, says the war in Ukraine shows how exposed generators and fuel runs have become near the front.

“The very first thing that happened in the war was every generator on the entire battlefield got annihilated,” John Webber, the company’s vice president of sales, told the DCNF.

Drones can find a running generator by its heat and noise, and the area they can reach has grown from eight to 10 miles at the start of the war to about 25 miles, Webber said.

“If you’ve got a heavy vehicle that can only drive at 30 miles an hour, you’re exposed for 50 minutes carrying fuel,” he said.

The nodes are built to work alongside generators, so a unit can plug a generator into a node’s built-in charger, fill its battery in about 90 minutes and then shut the generator off, Webber said.

“So we can charge very quickly, get that generator turned off, and now we can coast for the next 10 hours, which we’ve proven out on NTC,” he added, referring to the Army’s National Training Center.

Generators burn fuel most efficiently at about 80 percent of their rated output, Webber said, and charging a node lets a generator run near that level instead of idling on small loads such as “a Starlink and two laptops.”

The company is building three node sizes and expects the largest to cost $15,000 to $18,000 and the smallest, a 1-kilowatt unit, “well under $10,000,” he said.

“Because we’re attritable, we’re low cost,” he added. “If something gets lost, destroyed, or otherwise, nobody’s weeping. They’re just sending out another unit.”

The company is designing the nodes in the U.S., and it has no plans to make any key components outside the country, Webber said. The hardest part to find at home is the battery management system, the electronics that control a battery, he said, “because China has that locked up, people just keep buying the little BMSs [battery management systems] from China.”

New Use Energy’s current commercial units are made in China, Paul Shmotolokha, the company’s CEO, told the DCNF in a phone interview. For the next-generation version it is building for the Army, “we’re designing more for the supply chain, so it’ll be no Chinese parts,” he said.

“This program could create real jobs over time and support American component manufacturers in areas where we’ve ceded almost the entire market,” Shmotolokha said in September, according to NextGen Defense.

“We use Ukrainian sniper suit technology to wrap our cases if they’re operating in exposed environments, so that we shield from those IR [infrared] drones,” Shmotolokha told the DCNF, referring to cheap drones that can spot heat.

“Diesel pound for pound is great, but you can’t use it indoors, which means can’t hide it,” he said, adding that “drones hear generators.”

“However much power you need or energy you need, double it. You always need more,” Shmotolokha said.

DLA Energy sold 76.5 million barrels of fuel, or about 3.2 billion gallons, to all of its customers in fiscal 2025, according to the agency’s 2025 fact book.

(عکس از آرمین وایگل/ خبرگزاری فرانسه از طریق گتی ایماژ)
شرکت‌های آمریکایی در حال ساخت باتری‌ها، پهپادهای هیدروژنی و سوخت‌های داخلی هستند که می‌توانند نیرو‌های آمریکایی را در صورت قطع کردن عرضه خارجی به نیروهای آمریکایی حفظ کنند. شرکت‌ها تجهیزات خود را در نشست سالانه انجمن ارتش ایالات متحده که در 14 اکتبر به پایان رسید، به نمایش گذاشتند. 14، با استناد به داده های مستقل. (مرتبط: داده‌های نفتکش نشان می‌دهد که ممکن است بشکه‌های کمتر از آنچه تصور می‌شد از هرمز عبور کنند)
ژنرال مارک سیمرلی، مدیر آژانس لجستیک دفاعی (DLA)، در اجلاس لجستیک و انرژی دفاعی 2026 در سپتامبر 2026 گفت: «روزهای محیط‌های لجستیکی امن و قابل پیش‌بینی به پایان رسیده‌اند». وی افزود که انرژی و سوخت "هدف های با ارزش و عوامل تعیین کننده در موفقیت عملیات خواهند بود."
جردن گیلیس، دستیار وزیر ارتش در امور تاسیسات، انرژی و محیط زیست، در ماه مارس به کمیته فرعی خدمات مسلح مجلس گفت که در هند و اقیانوس آرام، بر اساس شهادت کتبی او، «تدارکات سوخت و مکان‌های جزیره آسیب‌پذیر چالش‌های انرژی منحصربه‌فردی را ایجاد می‌کنند». بازوی انرژی DLA در بیانیه ای به بنیاد Daily Caller News گفت: «از مارس تا سپتامبر 2026، DLA Energy تقریباً 2.17 میلیارد گالن سوخت را عمدتاً برای حمایت از وزارت جنگ خریداری کرد و تقریباً 122.7 میلیون گالن برای حمایت از ارتش ایالات متحده فروخت.

news.originalContent:
President Macron promises to increase security, but stops short of announcing a state of emergency or curfew.

Macron vows action against protest violence after crisis meeting over France unrest

French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed “anger and shame” over what he described as violent protesters’ attempts “to bring down the republic”.

In a televised address to the nation on Sunday, Macron promised that rioters and looters would “pay for their crimes”, after Saturday saw some of the worst urban violence in France in years.

The country’s Interior Ministry said that nearly 2,400 people were arrested on Saturday, with about 1,000 police and gendarmes injured.

Macron said there must be a distinction between protesters with “legitimate demands” and “those who destroyed, smashed, and looted”.

The president pledged to launch a “crisis unit” to provide “urgent aid … for those who are going through difficult moments”. He added that “lessons will be learned” after the destructive violence erupted this weekend.

“We need to be clear: yesterday, our law enforcement officers and officials, despite their professionalism, were subjected to unprecedented violence in several cities,” he said.

“I’ve asked the government to provide all the lessons learned and to be able to anticipate it to make sure that this does not happen again,” Macron said, adding: “We need unity, we need calm and respect.”

Reporting from Paris, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said Macron’s speech had “perhaps no surprises”.

“Whether it’s going to be enough to placate some people, I’m not really sure, because those who have been out protesting say they’re fed up of hearing these sorts of speeches by the French president,” Butler said.

The protests are quickly becoming a political football for parties vying for public support ahead of presidential elections next year.

Left-wing presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said the French government is “solely responsible” for the destruction during protests, and has “failed to organise the maintenance of public order”.

Far-right presidential hopeful Jordan Bardella called Macron’s Sunday speech “lamentable” and “cowardly”, saying the government has nothing left to offer the French people and “cannot even protect them”.
news.content:
رئیس‌جمهور مکرون قول افزایش امنیت را می‌دهد، اما از اعلام وضعیت اضطراری یا منع آمد و شد کوتاهی می‌کند. مکرون قول داد پس از نشست بحران در مورد ناآرامی‌های فرانسه، علیه خشونت اعتراضی اقدام کند.
امانوئل ماکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، نسبت به آنچه که او تلاش‌های خشونت‌آمیز معترضان برای «سقوط جمهوری» توصیف کرد، «خشم و شرم» را ابراز کرد. ماکرون روز یکشنبه در یک سخنرانی تلویزیونی خطاب به ملت وعده داد که آشوبگران و غارتگران «هزینه جنایات خود را خواهند پرداخت»، پس از اینکه شنبه شاهد بدترین خشونت‌های شهری در فرانسه در سال‌های اخیر بود. وزارت کشور این کشور گفت که نزدیک به 2400 نفر در روز شنبه دستگیر شدند و حدود 1000 پلیس و ژاندارم زخمی شدند. ماکرون گفت: باید بین معترضان با "خواسته های مشروع" و "کسانی که ویران کردند، شکستند و غارت کردند" تمایز وجود داشت. او افزود که پس از وقوع خشونت های مخرب در این آخر هفته، «درس هایی آموخته خواهد شد». ماکرون گفت: «ما باید شفاف باشیم: دیروز، افسران و مقامات مجری قانون ما، علی‌رغم حرفه‌ای بودن، در چندین شهر مورد خشونت بی‌سابقه‌ای قرار گرفتند.» ماکرون گفت: «از دولت خواسته‌ام تمام درس‌های آموخته شده را ارائه دهد و بتواند آن را پیش‌بینی کند تا مطمئن شود این اتفاق تکرار نمی‌شود.» ناتاشا باتلر، خبرنگار الجزیره در گزارشی از پاریس گفت که سخنرانی مکرون «شاید نه

news.originalContent:
یک سال پیش، یکی از سناتورهای باسابقه آمریکا چندان درباره دینا سنترها (مراکز داده) فکر نمی‌کرد.

اما اکنون، به گفته یکی از مشاورانش، او به‌طور منظم با اعضای دفتر خود درباره تاثیر این مراکز جلسه برگزار می‌کند و روی تدوین طرحی قانونی کار می‌کند که هدف آن مهار گسترش سریع مراکز داده در سراسر آمریکا است.

یکی از مشاوران ارشد سیاست‌گذاری این سناتور دموکرات به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «گاهی همین‌طور است؛ موضوعی ابتدا آرام و آهسته شروع می‌شود و بعد ناگهان شتاب می‌گیرد.» او به شرط ناشناس ماندن صحبت کرد، چون اجازه گفت‌وگو با رسانه‌ها را ندارد.

چرخش ۱۸۰ درجه‌ای توجه این سناتور تقریبا به‌طور کامل نتیجه موج فزاینده مخالفت‌های عمومی بود؛ موجی که سیاستمداران را در سراسر آمریکا وادار کرده برای عقب نماندن از آن دست به کار شوند.

افکار عمومی به‌تدریج علیه گسترش مراکز داده موضع گرفته است؛ ساختمان‌های عظیم و انبارمانندی که توان پردازشی مورد نیاز برای فعالیت‌های اینترنتی را در خود جای می‌دهند.

مراکز داده با ردیف‌های متعدد تراشه‌های رایانه‌ای، که گاهی ارتفاع تجهیزات آن‌ها به بیش از دو متر می‌رسد، دیگر فقط زیرساخت اینترنت نیستند. آن‌ها اکنون به نمود فیزیکی رشد سریع و انفجاری فناوری هوش مصنوعی و نگرانی‌های مختلفی تبدیل شده‌اند که مردم با آن مرتبط می‌دانند.

آنجلیتا سوریانو، ساکن ایندیانا، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «نمی‌خواهم موش آزمایشگاهی این ماجرا باشم.»

درست روبه‌روی خانه او، آمازون در حال ساخت یک مرکز داده جدید است. پس از تکمیل، این مجموعه متشکل از ۲۶ ساختمان بیش از ۲ کیلومتر مربع از محله محل زندگی او را در بر خواهد گرفت و ۷۸۲ ژنراتور دیزلی در آن به کار گرفته خواهد شد.

برخی مراکز داده حتی بزرگ‌ترند.

در اوهایو، پروژه مشترکی میان اوپن‌ای‌آی، انویدیا، اس‌بی انرژی و وزارت انرژی آمریکا قرار است مجموعه‌ای از مراکز داده بسازد که حدود شش مایل مربع، نزدیک به ۱۵/۵ کیلومتر مربع، وسعت خواهد داشت، تقریبا به اندازه بسیاری از شهرک‌های آمریکا.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اکنون حدود ۳ هزار مرکز داده در آمریکا فعال است و بر اساس گزارشی از مرکز پژوهشی پیو، این تعداد ممکن است طی چند سال آینده دو برابر شود.

ساخت مراکز داده عمدتا بر اساس مقررات و مجوزهای محلی انجام می‌شود، بنابراین قانون‌گذاران فدرال مانند سناتورهای آمریکا نقش محدودی در این روند دارند.

اما مخالفت با آن‌ها در آمریکا آن‌قدر سریع و شدید افزایش یافته که حالا سیاستمداران در همه سطوح تقریبا ناچارند موضعی مشخص اتخاذ کنند.

کلویی آتیو، مشاور سیاست‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی، گفت: «این فقط مسئله‌ای مربوط به جناح چپ نیست. در میان محافظه‌کاران هم مخالفت بسیار زیادی با مراکز داده وجود دارد. در هر دو حزب، هر کسی که موضع روشنی بیان کند و به آن پایبند بماند، می‌تواند از نظر سیاسی از آن بهره ببرد.»

مشاور سناتور آمریکایی که روی قانون‌گذاری مراکز داده کار می‌کند نیز ارزیابی مشابهی داشت.

او گفت: «اینجا نیاز مشخصی به سیاست‌گذاری وجود دارد و ما می‌خواهیم این خلا را پر کنیم. مخالفت بزرگی در سراسر کشور شکل گرفته است، مردم آثار مراکز داده را می‌بینند و از آن خوششان نمی‌آید.»

همین موضوع بسیاری از سیاستمداران کنگره، حتی جمهوری‌خواهان، را مستقیما در برابر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، قرار داده است؛ کسی که از رشد بدون محدودیت فناوری هوش مصنوعی حمایت کرده است.

ترامپ مخالفت با مراکز داده را «توطئه‌ای بیمارگونه» توصیف کرده و گفته است مردم و شهرهایی که می‌کوشند مانع ساخت آن‌ها شوند «عقب‌مانده و فقیر» هستند.

این موضع ترامپ برای سیاستمداران دموکراتی که می‌خواهند در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آرای شهروندان ناراضی یا مردد را جلب کنند، به فرصتی سیاسی تبدیل شده است.

بی‌بی‌سی با ساکنانی از ایندیانا، آریزونا، میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا و اورگن صحبت کرده است که همگی در سطح محلی علیه توسعه مراکز داده فعالیت می‌کنند.

آن‌ها نگرانی‌های مختلفی درباره این ساختمان‌ها مطرح کردند، از جمله اندازه آن‌ها، سروصدای ساخت‌وساز و فعالیت روزانه، اثر بر منابع هوا، آب و انرژی و همچنین سرعتی که به نظر می‌رسد مقام‌های محلی با آن پروژه‌ها را تصویب می‌کنند.

بر اساس پژوهش مؤسسه «دیتا سنتر واچ»، در چند ماه نخست سال جاری شمار گروه‌های محلی که علیه گسترش مراکز داده سازماندهی می‌کنند، بیش از دو برابر شد و به ۸۳۳ گروه رسید؛ گروه‌هایی که اکنون تقریبا در همه ایالت‌های آمریکا فعال‌اند.

«دیتا سنتر واچ» داده‌هایی را برای بازیگران صنعت هوش مصنوعی جمع‌آوری می‌کند و بخشی از شرکت نوپای هوش مصنوعی «۱۰ای لبز» (10a Labs) به شمار می‌رود.

استفانی مالدونادو، مدیر سیاسی سازمان «لوچا»، یک گروه سازمان‌دهی اجتماعی مستقر در ایالت آریزونا، مخالفت‌ها با گسترش مراکز داده را به داستان «داوود و جالوت» تشبیه می‌کند؛ جنبشی که به گفته او چند سال پیش آغاز شد.

مالدونادو افزود: «مردم از مدت‌ها پیش آماده بودند جلو آن را بگیرند. حالا عصبانی‌اند.»

نظرسنجی ملی تازه‌ای نشان می‌دهد پس از جنگ جاری ایران و مسائل مختلف اقتصادی، مقررات هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده از جمله موضوعات مهم برای رای‌دهندگان در این دوره انتخاباتی هستند.

طرفداران ساخت مراکز داده اغلب می‌گویند این پروژه‌ها شغل‌های بیشتر و با درآمد بالاتر برای جوامع محلی ایجاد می‌کنند.

اما پژوهش تازه موسسه بروکینگز، یک مرکز پژوهشی غیرحزبی، نشان داده است یک مرکز داده جدید بین ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ شغل محلی ایجاد می‌کند؛ رقمی که به گفته این موسسه «کمتر از چیزی است که حامیان صنعت ادعا می‌کنند».

این پروژه‌ها همچنین عملا تاثیری بر سطح دستمزدهای محلی ندارند.

منبع تصویر، Stephanie Maldonado

کتی هابز، فرماندار آریزونا، زمانی از حامیان چنین پروژه‌هایی بود، اما فشار عمومی باعث شد موضع خود را تغییر دهد.

او در ماه ژوئیه یک توقف سه‌ ساله برای اعطای هرگونه معافیت مالیاتی جدید به شرکت‌ها برای پروژه‌های مراکز داده تصویب کرد.

آریزونا تنها ایالتی نیست که سیاستمدارانش در واکنش به مخالفت عمومی با مراکز داده موضع خود را تغییر داده‌اند.

عبدال السید، نامزد دموکرات سنا در میشیگان، وضع مقررات جدید برای مراکز داده را به بخشی روشن از کارزار موفق خود در انتخابات مقدماتی سنا تبدیل کرده است.

در رقابت برای فرمانداری جورجیا نیز یک نامزد دموکرات که خواستار توقف توسعه مراکز داده است، در نظرسنجی‌ها رقابتی بسیار نزدیک با نامزد جمهوری‌خواهی دارد که با چنین توقفی مخالف است.

جان هوستد، سناتور جمهوری‌خواه اوهایو، که برای حفظ کرسی خود در برابر شرود براون، نامزد دموکرات، رقابت می‌کند نیز مجبور شده موضعش را تغییر دهد.

نظرسنجی‌های اخیر نشان داده‌اند اکثریت رای‌دهندگان اوهایو، فارغ از وابستگی حزبی، با مراکز داده مخالف‌اند.

هوستد حمایت خود را تعدیل کرده و گفته است تصمیم درباره ورود این مراکز باید بر عهده شهروندان محلی و مقام‌های منتخب باشد.

در مقابل، براون در کارزار انتخاباتی خود بر مخالفت با مراکز داده جدید تاکید کرده است. در نظرسنجی‌های اخیر او از هوستد جلوتر بوده است.

مشکلات هوستد در اوهایو باعث شد «کمیته ملی سناتوری جمهوری‌خواهان»، یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای جذب کمک مالی برای جمهوری‌خواهان سنا، در یادداشتی خصوصی بنویسد که سیاستمداران جمهوری‌خواه باید نحوه صحبت با رای‌دهندگان درباره مراکز داده را کاملا بازتعریف کنند.

این کمیته افزود: «این موضوع به یکی از مسائل کمتر دیده‌شده اما مهم کل چرخه انتخاباتی تبدیل شده است.»

تگزاس شاید روشن‌ترین نمونه‌ای باشد که نشان می‌دهد مخالفت عمومی چگونه حتی برای سیاستمداران به‌شدت طرفدار کسب‌وکار به موضوعی اجتناب‌ناپذیر تبدیل شده است.

بر اساس داده‌های پیو، اکنون نزدیک به ۳۰۰ مرکز داده در این ایالت فعال‌اند و ۱۷۰ مرکز دیگر نیز برای ساخت برنامه‌ریزی شده‌اند.

گرگ ابوت، فرماندار جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، در پایان سال گذشته با افتخار گفته بود تگزاس به دلیل تعداد مراکز داده خود «مرکز توسعه هوش مصنوعی» است.

اما تنها چند ماه بعد عقب‌نشینی کرد و به نگرانی‌هایی درباره «ایمنی و کیفیت زندگی» اشاره کرد.

این مسئله ممکن است در رقابت پیش‌روی سنا در این ایالت نیز نقش داشته باشد.

کارزار جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات، خواستار پایان دادن به «توافق‌های مالیاتی ویژه» برای شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری است.

او اکنون در رقابت برای کرسی‌ که از نظر تاریخی در اختیار جمهوری‌خواهان بوده، در برابر کن پکستون، دادستان کل جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، قرار دارد.

پکستون در مصاحبه‌ای در اواخر سپتامبر گفت هنوز «فضای باز فراوانی در تگزاس وجود دارد که می‌توانیم مراکز داده را آنجا بسازیم».

بسیاری از اقدامات یا پیشنهادهایی که سیاستمداران برای پاسخ به نگرانی این رای‌دهندگان مطرح کرده‌اند، موقتی هستند.

برای مثال، بیشتر ممنوعیت‌ها یا توقف‌های موقت پس از یک تا سه سال پایان خواهند یافت.

ممکن است تا زمان پایان این توقف‌ها فضای سیاسی تغییر کرده باشد و شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری و هوش مصنوعی دوباره بتوانند مطابق خواسته خود پروژه‌هایشان را پیش ببرند.

اما فعلا احساسات عمومی نسبت به آن‌ها شدید است.

بالاجی تاماباتولا، مدیرعامل «باراپان» در حال توسعه یک مرکز داده و مجموعه فناوری در زمینی به وسعت به ۷۰۰ جریب در لیبرتی تگزاس است.

او به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که با وجود آنکه این تاسیسات به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که آب مورد نیاز خود را از طریق جمع‌آوری آب باران تامین کنند و انرژی مورد نیازشان را نیز خود تولید کنند، که رویکردی روزبه‌روز رایج‌تر در پروژه‌های بزرگ مراکز داده است، بسیاری از ساکنان منطقه از همان ابتدا با این طرح مخالفت کرده‌اند.

او گفت: «از همان لحظه اول سطح تنش آن‌قدر بالاست که تقریبا حتی نمی‌توان با ارائه واقعیت‌ها از این دیوار عبور کرد.»

تاماباتولا گفت در یک نشست اجتماعی اخیر تلاش کرده است با زنی که به‌شدت با پروژه مخالف بود، رو‌در‌رو صحبت کند.

او گفت: این زن مستقیم در چشمانم نگاه کرد و گفت: «"از ایالت من برو بیرون."»

آنجلیتا سوریانو، ساکن ایندیانا، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «نمی‌خواهم موش آزمایشگاهی این ماجرا باشم.»

درست روبه‌روی خانه او، آمازون در حال ساخت یک مرکز داده جدید است. پس از تکمیل، این مجموعه متشکل از ۲۶ ساختمان بیش از ۲ کیلومتر مربع از محله محل زندگی او را در بر خواهد گرفت و ۷۸۲ ژنراتور دیزلی در آن به کار گرفته خواهد شد.

برخی مراکز داده حتی بزرگ‌ترند.

در اوهایو، پروژه مشترکی میان اوپن‌ای‌آی، انویدیا، اس‌بی انرژی و وزارت انرژی آمریکا قرار است مجموعه‌ای از مراکز داده بسازد که حدود شش مایل مربع، نزدیک به ۱۵/۵ کیلومتر مربع، وسعت خواهد داشت، تقریبا به اندازه بسیاری از شهرک‌های آمریکا.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اکنون حدود ۳ هزار مرکز داده در آمریکا فعال است و بر اساس گزارشی از مرکز پژوهشی پیو، این تعداد ممکن است طی چند سال آینده دو برابر شود.

ساخت مراکز داده عمدتا بر اساس مقررات و مجوزهای محلی انجام می‌شود، بنابراین قانون‌گذاران فدرال مانند سناتورهای آمریکا نقش محدودی در این روند دارند.

اما مخالفت با آن‌ها در آمریکا آن‌قدر سریع و شدید افزایش یافته که حالا سیاستمداران در همه سطوح تقریبا ناچارند موضعی مشخص اتخاذ کنند.

کلویی آتیو، مشاور سیاست‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی، گفت: «این فقط مسئله‌ای مربوط به جناح چپ نیست. در میان محافظه‌کاران هم مخالفت بسیار زیادی با مراکز داده وجود دارد. در هر دو حزب، هر کسی که موضع روشنی بیان کند و به آن پایبند بماند، می‌تواند از نظر سیاسی از آن بهره ببرد.»

مشاور سناتور آمریکایی که روی قانون‌گذاری مراکز داده کار می‌کند نیز ارزیابی مشابهی داشت.

او گفت: «اینجا نیاز مشخصی به سیاست‌گذاری وجود دارد و ما می‌خواهیم این خلا را پر کنیم. مخالفت بزرگی در سراسر کشور شکل گرفته است، مردم آثار مراکز داده را می‌بینند و از آن خوششان نمی‌آید.»

همین موضوع بسیاری از سیاستمداران کنگره، حتی جمهوری‌خواهان، را مستقیما در برابر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، قرار داده است؛ کسی که از رشد بدون محدودیت فناوری هوش مصنوعی حمایت کرده است.

ترامپ مخالفت با مراکز داده را «توطئه‌ای بیمارگونه» توصیف کرده و گفته است مردم و شهرهایی که می‌کوشند مانع ساخت آن‌ها شوند «عقب‌مانده و فقیر» هستند.

این موضع ترامپ برای سیاستمداران دموکراتی که می‌خواهند در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آرای شهروندان ناراضی یا مردد را جلب کنند، به فرصتی سیاسی تبدیل شده است.

بی‌بی‌سی با ساکنانی از ایندیانا، آریزونا، میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا و اورگن صحبت کرده است که همگی در سطح محلی علیه توسعه مراکز داده فعالیت می‌کنند.

آن‌ها نگرانی‌های مختلفی درباره این ساختمان‌ها مطرح کردند، از جمله اندازه آن‌ها، سروصدای ساخت‌وساز و فعالیت روزانه، اثر بر منابع هوا، آب و انرژی و همچنین سرعتی که به نظر می‌رسد مقام‌های محلی با آن پروژه‌ها را تصویب می‌کنند.

بر اساس پژوهش مؤسسه «دیتا سنتر واچ»، در چند ماه نخست سال جاری شمار گروه‌های محلی که علیه گسترش مراکز داده سازماندهی می‌کنند، بیش از دو برابر شد و به ۸۳۳ گروه رسید؛ گروه‌هایی که اکنون تقریبا در همه ایالت‌های آمریکا فعال‌اند.

«دیتا سنتر واچ» داده‌هایی را برای بازیگران صنعت هوش مصنوعی جمع‌آوری می‌کند و بخشی از شرکت نوپای هوش مصنوعی «۱۰ای لبز» (10a Labs) به شمار می‌رود.

استفانی مالدونادو، مدیر سیاسی سازمان «لوچا»، یک گروه سازمان‌دهی اجتماعی مستقر در ایالت آریزونا، مخالفت‌ها با گسترش مراکز داده را به داستان «داوود و جالوت» تشبیه می‌کند؛ جنبشی که به گفته او چند سال پیش آغاز شد.

مالدونادو افزود: «مردم از مدت‌ها پیش آماده بودند جلو آن را بگیرند. حالا عصبانی‌اند.»

نظرسنجی ملی تازه‌ای نشان می‌دهد پس از جنگ جاری ایران و مسائل مختلف اقتصادی، مقررات هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده از جمله موضوعات مهم برای رای‌دهندگان در این دوره انتخاباتی هستند.

طرفداران ساخت مراکز داده اغلب می‌گویند این پروژه‌ها شغل‌های بیشتر و با درآمد بالاتر برای جوامع محلی ایجاد می‌کنند.

اما پژوهش تازه موسسه بروکینگز، یک مرکز پژوهشی غیرحزبی، نشان داده است یک مرکز داده جدید بین ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ شغل محلی ایجاد می‌کند؛ رقمی که به گفته این موسسه «کمتر از چیزی است که حامیان صنعت ادعا می‌کنند».

این پروژه‌ها همچنین عملا تاثیری بر سطح دستمزدهای محلی ندارند.

منبع تصویر، Stephanie Maldonado

کتی هابز، فرماندار آریزونا، زمانی از حامیان چنین پروژه‌هایی بود، اما فشار عمومی باعث شد موضع خود را تغییر دهد.

او در ماه ژوئیه یک توقف سه‌ ساله برای اعطای هرگونه معافیت مالیاتی جدید به شرکت‌ها برای پروژه‌های مراکز داده تصویب کرد.

آریزونا تنها ایالتی نیست که سیاستمدارانش در واکنش به مخالفت عمومی با مراکز داده موضع خود را تغییر داده‌اند.

عبدال السید، نامزد دموکرات سنا در میشیگان، وضع مقررات جدید برای مراکز داده را به بخشی روشن از کارزار موفق خود در انتخابات مقدماتی سنا تبدیل کرده است.

در رقابت برای فرمانداری جورجیا نیز یک نامزد دموکرات که خواستار توقف توسعه مراکز داده است، در نظرسنجی‌ها رقابتی بسیار نزدیک با نامزد جمهوری‌خواهی دارد که با چنین توقفی مخالف است.

جان هوستد، سناتور جمهوری‌خواه اوهایو، که برای حفظ کرسی خود در برابر شرود براون، نامزد دموکرات، رقابت می‌کند نیز مجبور شده موضعش را تغییر دهد.

نظرسنجی‌های اخیر نشان داده‌اند اکثریت رای‌دهندگان اوهایو، فارغ از وابستگی حزبی، با مراکز داده مخالف‌اند.

هوستد حمایت خود را تعدیل کرده و گفته است تصمیم درباره ورود این مراکز باید بر عهده شهروندان محلی و مقام‌های منتخب باشد.

در مقابل، براون در کارزار انتخاباتی خود بر مخالفت با مراکز داده جدید تاکید کرده است. در نظرسنجی‌های اخیر او از هوستد جلوتر بوده است.

مشکلات هوستد در اوهایو باعث شد «کمیته ملی سناتوری جمهوری‌خواهان»، یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای جذب کمک مالی برای جمهوری‌خواهان سنا، در یادداشتی خصوصی بنویسد که سیاستمداران جمهوری‌خواه باید نحوه صحبت با رای‌دهندگان درباره مراکز داده را کاملا بازتعریف کنند.

این کمیته افزود: «این موضوع به یکی از مسائل کمتر دیده‌شده اما مهم کل چرخه انتخاباتی تبدیل شده است.»

تگزاس شاید روشن‌ترین نمونه‌ای باشد که نشان می‌دهد مخالفت عمومی چگونه حتی برای سیاستمداران به‌شدت طرفدار کسب‌وکار به موضوعی اجتناب‌ناپذیر تبدیل شده است.

بر اساس داده‌های پیو، اکنون نزدیک به ۳۰۰ مرکز داده در این ایالت فعال‌اند و ۱۷۰ مرکز دیگر نیز برای ساخت برنامه‌ریزی شده‌اند.

گرگ ابوت، فرماندار جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، در پایان سال گذشته با افتخار گفته بود تگزاس به دلیل تعداد مراکز داده خود «مرکز توسعه هوش مصنوعی» است.

اما تنها چند ماه بعد عقب‌نشینی کرد و به نگرانی‌هایی درباره «ایمنی و کیفیت زندگی» اشاره کرد.

این مسئله ممکن است در رقابت پیش‌روی سنا در این ایالت نیز نقش داشته باشد.

کارزار جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات، خواستار پایان دادن به «توافق‌های مالیاتی ویژه» برای شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری است.

او اکنون در رقابت برای کرسی‌ که از نظر تاریخی در اختیار جمهوری‌خواهان بوده، در برابر کن پکستون، دادستان کل جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، قرار دارد.

پکستون در مصاحبه‌ای در اواخر سپتامبر گفت هنوز «فضای باز فراوانی در تگزاس وجود دارد که می‌توانیم مراکز داده را آنجا بسازیم».

بسیاری از اقدامات یا پیشنهادهایی که سیاستمداران برای پاسخ به نگرانی این رای‌دهندگان مطرح کرده‌اند، موقتی هستند.

برای مثال، بیشتر ممنوعیت‌ها یا توقف‌های موقت پس از یک تا سه سال پایان خواهند یافت.

ممکن است تا زمان پایان این توقف‌ها فضای سیاسی تغییر کرده باشد و شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری و هوش مصنوعی دوباره بتوانند مطابق خواسته خود پروژه‌هایشان را پیش ببرند.

اما فعلا احساسات عمومی نسبت به آن‌ها شدید است.

بالاجی تاماباتولا، مدیرعامل «باراپان» در حال توسعه یک مرکز داده و مجموعه فناوری در زمینی به وسعت به ۷۰۰ جریب در لیبرتی تگزاس است.

او به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که با وجود آنکه این تاسیسات به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که آب مورد نیاز خود را از طریق جمع‌آوری آب باران تامین کنند و انرژی مورد نیازشان را نیز خود تولید کنند، که رویکردی روزبه‌روز رایج‌تر در پروژه‌های بزرگ مراکز داده است، بسیاری از ساکنان منطقه از همان ابتدا با این طرح مخالفت کرده‌اند.

او گفت: «از همان لحظه اول سطح تنش آن‌قدر بالاست که تقریبا حتی نمی‌توان با ارائه واقعیت‌ها از این دیوار عبور کرد.»

تاماباتولا گفت در یک نشست اجتماعی اخیر تلاش کرده است با زنی که به‌شدت با پروژه مخالف بود، رو‌در‌رو صحبت کند.

او گفت: این زن مستقیم در چشمانم نگاه کرد و گفت: «"از ایالت من برو بیرون."»

news.originalContent:
Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images

A fake drug commercial, a show-tune parody and politicians dancing to rapper Kendrick Lamar are all part of this cycle’s artificial intelligence-powered midterm pitch to voters.

Campaigns and outside groups had spent nearly $80 million on at least 164 political ads made or enhanced with AI as of Sept. 4, the Wesleyan Media Project found. As the Nov. 3 Election Day approaches, AI ads have been used in key senate and governor races, and some have faced ridicule from critics online who call them “AI slop.”

Citizens for Sanity, a group advised by former Trump deputy White House counsel Gene Hamilton, put six figures behind an AI ad that turns Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico into Julie Andrews’ beloved character, Maria, from “The Sound of Music,” the Daily Caller first reported on June 9. (RELATED: Anthropic’s AI Sent Police A False Report Of A Homicide)

The AI-generated Talarico, depicted in a video posted by the Daily Caller on X, belts out new lyrics to the musical’s number “My Favorite Things” about gender transitions for minors, which is a callback to his comment that he loves “the trans children,” in an Aug. 2, 2023, interview on A Superbloom Podcast.

Months after winning the Democratic Senate nomination over Texas Rep. Jasmine Crockett, Talarico stated on a June episode of another podcast that he opposed child sex changes.

“Boys in white dresses with blue satin sashes. Girls dosed with hormones til they grow mustaches. Changing the gender of all your offspring. These are a few of my favorite things,” the AI-generated Talarico sings.

NEW: The Trump-aligned org Citizens for Sanity is dropping a six-figure ad buy in the Texas Senate race. The ad is a 15 second clip of AI-generated James Talarico singing a "trans kids" rendition of “Favorite Things." Obtained first by @DailyCaller: https://t.co/JNY8vxYueG

“Citizens for sanity” as they make up really weird fake AI fetish videos of a man in dresses,” said one X user in response to the ad.

“Keep burning money,” Rogue DNC said on X in response to the video.

Republican New York gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman posted an AI-generated attack ad to X on Sept. 1 that showed incumbent Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in a mock drug commercial for “delusion pills.”

“Introducing Kathy, the political delusion pill for New Yorkers who would rather not think about what four more years could actually cost them,” the ad states, showing Hochul working in an outdoor garden with Mamdani.

.@KathyHochul and @ZohranKMamdani think they can cure New York’s cost-of-living crisis with excuses, empty promises, and "delusion pills." The real side effects of their policies aren’t a joke: 48 utility rate hikes, higher taxes, uncontrollable government spending, and businesses fleeing our state every single day. I have a different plan for New York. As Governor, I will deliver zero state income tax on your first $50,000, $100,000 for joint filers, cut your utility bills in half, and end the government waste. Don’t let them tax New York into the ground. Help me make New York affordable again.

State Democrats filed a Board of Elections complaint on Aug. 10, arguing Blakeman’s AI ads were “materially deceptive media,” while Blakeman, the Nassau County Executive, insisted to News10 that voters “like satire.”

The Front Line Action, a Texas super PAC, tied to Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, poured upward of $90,000 into an AI-generated ad targeting Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, according to FEC filings.

Titled “Family Values,” the ad depicts an AI interpretation of El-Sayed playing a board game with his half-sister and streamer Hasan Piker as they pass around cards reading “Death to America” and “Celebrate 9/11.” In the ad, a narrator warns that “El-Sayed isn’t playing games, and his family values are wrong for Michigan.”

The ad was posted to YouTube on Sept. 11 and features women in burqas.

“[Republicans] are so desperate that they are resorting to cheap AI generated ads filled with falsehoods and bad faith attacks,” Cole Wozniak, El-Sayed’s campaign spokesman said in a statement to CNN.

Republican Tennessee Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s campaign account on X shared an AI clip Tuesday of her performing a rendition of Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” imitating the rapper’s 2025 Super Bowl halftime performance. Dancing alongside her are fellow Tennessee Republicans Sen. Bill Hagerty, Rep. Tim Burchett, state Sen. Brent Taylor and former Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, dressed as his wrestling persona Kane.

“You know, there is a county commissioner that made the video and put it up … we reposted it, and it’s a funsie. Everybody get out and vote!” Blackburn told WZTV, according to the National Desk.

Tomorrow. Ready to roll. https://t.co/YiWREmkjyx

“What in the absolute fucking AI slop is this?” an X user wrote in response to the video.

“Boomer thinks AI makes her look cool,” Adam Kinzinger, former Republican Illinois Rep wrote on X about the ad.

The ads may grab attention, but it’s unclear they change voters’ minds.

“Whether this is a complete game changer, I’m skeptical that these ads are any more persuasive than the old-fashioned political ad,” Travis Ridout, co-director of the Wesleyan Media Project, told USA Today.

Republican candidates and allied groups were behind 83 percent of AI ad spending tracked by the project. However, with no federal requirement to disclose AI use, actual spending on AI ads may be even higher.

news.originalContent:
A government at war with its critics – from young protesters to the media.

A wave of youth-led protests has returned to the streets of India’s capital, Delhi, after media reports revealed that the Electoral Commission removed about 130 million names from voter lists.

These protests differ from the unrest that exploded in July, though, by the attacks on the media.

Dozens of journalists and content creators have been detained, assaulted or blocked from doing their jobs. But tightening the screws on critical reporting doesn’t appear to be working, as a new generation rises to challenge the government.

Contributors:
Saba Naqvi – Author and journalist
Smita Sharma – Multimedia journalist
Shyam Meera Singh – Founder, Strike Originals
Sushant Singh – Lecturer, Yale University

Pakistan has declared a state of emergency in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following protests calling for the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan.

The state’s response has followed a familiar pattern: A media blackout and internet shutdown, while casting protesters as rebels.

It’s been more than three years since Jair Bolsonaro fell from power, yet the right-wing movement he started is still without a clear leader. Into that gap has stepped a new crop of young evangelical political influencers, who are tapping into a decades-old religious media machine to build their audience.

Their viral content ricochets across social feeds, mobilising followers and voters in ways old-school politicians just can’t match.

The Listening Post’s Nicholas Muirhead reports on Brazil’s evangelical influencers and the political space they are looking to take over.

Featuring: 
Anna Virginia Balloussier – Journalist, Folha De Sao Paulo
Caro Evangelista – Executive director, Iser
Magali Cunha – Editor-in-chief, Berreia Project
news.content:
دولت در حال جنگ با منتقدان خود - از معترضان جوان گرفته تا رسانه‌ها. پس از گزارش‌های رسانه‌ها مبنی بر حذف حدود 130 میلیون نام از فهرست رأی‌دهندگان توسط کمیسیون انتخابات، موجی از اعتراضات به رهبری جوانان به خیابان‌های دهلی، پایتخت هند بازگشت. ده‌ها روزنامه‌نگار و تولیدکنندگان محتوا بازداشت شده‌اند، مورد حمله قرار گرفته‌اند یا از انجام وظایف خود جلوگیری کرده‌اند. اما به نظر نمی رسد سفت کردن پیچ ها بر روی گزارش های انتقادی کارساز باشد، زیرا نسل جدیدی برای به چالش کشیدن دولت برمی خیزد. مشارکت کنندگان:
صبا نقوی – نویسنده و روزنامه نگار
اسمیتا شارما – روزنامه نگار چند رسانه ای
شیام میرا سینگ - موسس، Strike Originals
سوشانت سینگ - مدرس دانشگاه ییل پاکستان در پی اعتراضاتی که خواستار آزادی عمران خان نخست وزیر سابق زندانی شده بودند، در استان خیبر پختونخوا در شمال غربی این کشور وضعیت فوق العاده اعلام کرد. واکنش این ایالت از یک الگوی آشنا پیروی کرد: قطع رسانه ها و قطع اینترنت، در حالی که معترضان را به عنوان شورشیان معرفی می کرد. بیش از سه سال از سقوط ژایر بولسونارو از قدرت می گذرد، با این حال جنبش جناح راستی که او آغاز کرد هنوز بدون رهبر مشخص است. در این شکاف، گروه جدیدی از تأثیرگذاران سیاسی انجیلی جوان قدم گذاشته‌اند که از ماشین رسانه‌ای مذهبی دهه‌ها استفاده می‌کنند تا مخاطبان خود را بسازند. محتوای ویروسی آنها در فیدهای اجتماعی کمانه می‌کند و پیروان و رأی‌دهندگان را به روش‌هایی بسیج می‌کند.

Weeks of student protests in France have grown into some of the worst unrest in Europe in recent years.

news.originalContent:
Image not from story(Photo by Chris Hondros/Getty Images)

A Catholic priest in Ecuador was killed when a crucifix broke loose from the wall and fell on him during a Mass he was streaming live.

Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading a service on Saturday, Oct. 17, at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil when the heavy cross gave way, according to Newsweek. The fixture tore loose about 27 minutes into the online broadcast.

The wooden cross had hung on the wall behind the altar. Footage of the Mass captured it toppling onto the priest as he spoke to worshippers. Congregants rushed forward to help him. He died from his injuries.

The cause of the collapse remained unknown, Newsweek reported. No official statement had said whether structural damage or faulty fittings contributed. (RELATED: Rider’s Fatal Fall Captured In Rollercoaster Souvenir Photo: REPORT)

The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed the priest’s death in a post on social media on Sunday. The archdiocese said he had passed into God’s presence and asked that he be granted eternal rest. It also sent condolences to his family and to his Redemptorist community.

Sánchez Molinari served as parish priest of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in the city’s Central Vicariate, according to Newsweek. He belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, the order widely known as the Redemptorists. He streamed his Masses regularly through his own social media accounts and a YouTube channel. Earlier in his ministry he had worked in Vinces, in Los Ríos Province, according to Newseek, citing Guayaquil News.

The Italian priest St. Alphonsus Liguori founded the Redemptorist order in 1732. The congregation has long concentrated its work among poor and isolated communities. Its members now total roughly 4,500 across 82 countries.

By Sunday, the church had still offered no public account of what caused the fall, according to IBTimes.

تصویر از داستان نیست (عکس از کریس هندروس/گتی ایماژ)
یک کشیش کاتولیک در اکوادور هنگامی که یک صلیب از دیوار جدا شد و بر روی او افتاد کشته شد. به گفته Newsweek، پدر پاتریسیو آلفردو سانچز مولیناری در روز شنبه، 17 اکتبر، در کلیسای بانوی کمک دائمی در گوایاکیل در حال رهبری یک مراسم بود که صلیب سنگین جای خود را گرفت. این برنامه حدود 27 دقیقه پس از پخش آنلاین پاره شد. صلیب چوبی به دیوار پشت محراب آویزان شده بود. تصاویری از مراسم توده نشان می‌دهد که هنگام صحبت با عبادت‌کنندگان، روی کشیش فرو می‌رود. جماعت برای کمک به او هجوم آوردند. نیوزویک گزارش داد که او بر اثر جراحات جان خود را از دست داد. علت سقوط ناشناخته باقی مانده است. هیچ بیانیه رسمی نگفته است که آیا آسیب ساختاری یا اتصالات معیوب در این امر نقش داشته است یا خیر. (مرتبط: سقوط مرگبار رایدر در عکس یادگاری ترن هوایی ثبت شد: گزارش) اسقف نشین گوایاکیل روز یکشنبه در پستی در شبکه های اجتماعی مرگ کشیش را تایید کرد. اسقف اعظم گفت که او در محضر خداوند قرار گرفته و از او خواسته است که به او آرامش ابدی عطا شود. به گزارش نیوزویک، سانچز مولیناری به عنوان کشیش محله بانوی یاری دائمی در معاونت مرکزی شهر خدمت کرد. او به جماعت نجات دهنده اقدس تعلق داشت، گروهی که به طور گسترده به عنوان رستگاران شناخته می شود. او مراسم توده های خود را به طور منظم از طریق حساب های رسانه های اجتماعی خود و یک کانال یوتیوب پخش می کرد. اوایل در او

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images)

Israeli officials reportedly urged Qatar for years to keep sending money into Hamas-controlled Gaza.

Letters top Israeli security officials sent to Qatari leaders show Israel pushed for and helped run a program which moved close to $2 billion into Gaza, TIME reported Sunday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is running in Israel’s Oct. 27 national elections and was endorsed Sunday by President Donald Trump, has tried to distance himself from the payments, according to the outlet.

Letters obtained by TIME reveal Israel played a bigger role in the payments than Netanyahu has acknowledged.https://t.co/M1oyRf1mFl

Then-Mossad Director Yossi Cohen thanked Qatar’s emir, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in a 2020 letter for the “humanitarian aid efforts that the State of Qatar has provided the last few years to the Gaza Strip,” according to the outlet.

“Undoubtedly, these humanitarian efforts have played a crucial role in improving the humanitarian situation within the Gaza Strip, and ensuring stability and safety in the region,” Cohen wrote.

That same year, R. L. Maoz, who served on Netanyahu’s National Security Council, urged Qatari officials to keep the payments going even as the Israeli government criticized them in public, according to the outlet. “We reiterate the importance of continuing to transfer the Qatari humanitarian financial assistance through the existing mechanism,” Maoz wrote. (RELATED: Israeli Opposition Accuses Netanyahu Of Being Too Pro-Palestine)

Neither the Embassy of Israel in the United States nor the State of Qatar’s International Media Office immediately responded to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s requests for comment.

Then-Mossad Director David Barnea met with Qatari officials in September 2023, weeks before Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel, The New York Times reported in December 2023, citing several people familiar with the talks. Asked whether Israel wanted the payments to continue, Barnea responded affirmatively, according to the outlet.

While Netanyahu’s office did not respond to a request for comment from TIME, he told the outlet in 2024 the payments were intended to keep Gaza from collapsing. “The reason that successive governments agreed to that is that we wanted to make sure that Gaza has a functioning civilian administration to avoid humanitarian collapse,” he said.

A spokesperson for Qatar’s International Media Office, meanwhile, told TIME that all of the country’s aid went through Israel on its way into Gaza. “If any funding reached Hamas, as alleged by individuals and groups with political agendas against Qatar, the responsibility lies with Israel, which oversaw the delivery and created the mechanism,” the spokesperson reportedly said.

Qatar and several other Arab nations are working with Trump administration envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on a plan to restore Gaza’s basic services and end its reliance on armed Islamist groups, TIME reported.

news.originalContent:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Sunday when NBC News’ Kristen Welker asked why President Donald Trump is “rewarding a dictator” by waiving Russia sanctions.

Bessent said on “Meet the Press” that no sanctions were lifted and that European countries are still paying Russia for its energy. Trump effectively waived a law that would have added more sanctions, Bessent said, and the only thing lifted was the embargo on Russian diesel.

“No one has been tougher on Russian sanctions than President Trump,” Bessent said, pointing to Trump’s sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, Russia’s two largest energy companies. (RELATED: ‘No, We Haven’t’: Chris Wright Fires Back When Asked If Trump Admin Let Americans Down At Pump)

“But you then are pushing for even tougher sanctions,” Welker countered.

“But Kristen, we did the toughest sanctions,” the secretary said as he and the NBC News host continued to talk over each other.

“But why lift them now. What has [Russian President Vladimir] Putin done to deserve sanctions relief now?” Welker asked.

“Kristen, that’s not true. No sanctions were lifted on Friday,” Bessent insisted. “No sanctions were lifted.”

“There was a law that was supposed to put more sanctions in place. The president effectively waived that,” Welker pointed out.

Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving the Russian sanctions and tariffs required under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which he signed into law Sept. 18.

The law, named for the late Republican South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham, directs the president to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from the top five importers of Russian oil and gas and up to 500 percent on goods imported from Russia. The Senate passed it 86-11 on Aug. 7, and the House passed it 262-159 in September.

Bessent again ensured Welker that “no sanctions were lifted,” and that the “only thing that has been lifted was the diesel embargo.”

Also during the exchange, Welker told Bessent that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had told her the move “is a big support for Putin” and asked, “Why is the president rewarding a dictator who invaded Ukraine?”

“President Trump has made it clear he wants the killing to stop,” Bessent responded, adding that the law gives the president 60 days to assess the situation.

He then turned to Europe, saying European countries have given Russia Putin more money than they have given Ukraine.

“They continue to gorge on Russian energy,” Bessent said. (RELATED: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin Runs Into The Ban Congress Passed On Russian Energy)

The secretary said 136 of the 140 cargoes that left one Russian facility in the first six months of the year went to Europe, worth more than $8 billion. He said he asked European allies in the spring to join the U.S. in putting secondary tariffs on China and India and that they refused. “So why should the U.S. bear the burden?” he asked.

Welker then played a clip from Bessent’s January 2025 confirmation hearing, in which he said the Biden administration had been worried about raising U.S. energy prices during an election season. “Is President Trump doing what you accused President Biden of doing?” she asked.

“Kristen, the sanctions were double the Biden administration in an act of incredible bravery,” he replied. “Double the sanctions on the way out in January 2025.”

Bessent also said during the interview that the United Kingdom waived its own embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude in May, asking, “where’s the outrage for the rest of the world?”

“The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine,” he added.
news.content:
اسکات بسنت، وزیر خزانه داری روز یکشنبه هنگامی که کریستن ولکر، خبرنگار ان بی سی نیوز پرسید، چرا رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ با چشم پوشی از تحریم های روسیه، به دیکتاتور پاداش می دهد، پاسخ داد. بسنت گفت که ترامپ عملا قانونی را که تحریم‌های بیشتری را اضافه می‌کرد، کنار گذاشت و تنها چیزی که برداشته شد، تحریم گازوئیل روسیه بود. بسنت با اشاره به تحریم های ترامپ علیه روس نفت و لوک اویل، دو شرکت بزرگ انرژی روسیه، گفت: «هیچ کس به اندازه رئیس جمهور ترامپ در قبال تحریم های روسیه سختگیرانه نبوده است. (مرتبط: "نه، ما نداشتیم": کریس رایت وقتی از او پرسیده شد که آیا مدیر ترامپ آمریکایی ها را در پمپ ناامید می کند، پاسخ داد)
ولکر در پاسخ گفت: «اما شما برای تحریم‌های شدیدتر فشار می‌آورید. وزیر در حالی که او و مجری ان‌بی‌سی نیوز به گفتگو درباره یکدیگر ادامه می‌دادند، گفت: «اما کریستن، ما سخت‌ترین تحریم‌ها را انجام دادیم. اما چرا اکنون آنها را لغو کنیم. پوتین [ولادیمیر رئیس‌جمهور روسیه] چه کرده است که اکنون مستحق لغو تحریم‌ها باشد؟» ولکر پرسید: "کریستن، این درست نیست. هیچ تحریمی در روز جمعه لغو نشد." هیچ تحریمی برداشته نشد.»
قانونی وجود داشت که قرار بود تحریم های بیشتری را اعمال کند. رئیس جمهور عملاً از آن چشم پوشی کرد.
